label: input token x (copy phase, plus x at t=0)
explanation: Token detector for input x. Fires strongly (about 0.6-1.0 of max) whenever x is fed back as input during the copy phase, and weakly (about 0.13) when x is the first original token (t=0). Precision on dev is 1.0. During the original phase, x after t=0 gives at most weak activations (about 0.1-0.2) and is usually inactive. The rest of the misses are rare weak activations (<0.2) on other tokens (e, p, s, g), carrying about 1.6% of the mass. In the top examples, magnitude is highest for x at early copy positions (recall_idx 1-2) and lower for x later in the copy. It does not fire on the delimiter or on any other token at meaningful strength.

issues: Minor: on test, x fed back in the copy phase alone gives precision 1.0, recall 0.78 and mass recall 0.954. x at t=0 gives precision 1.0, recall 0.14 and mass recall 0.03. Both match the explanation, and the t=0 firing is reliable, not occasional.
Minor: x at an original-phase step after t=0 fires 3.2% of the time and carries about 0.6% of the activation mass. That matches 'usually inactive, weak when it fires'.

Minor: other tokens in the copy phase account for 4.9% of active steps but only about 1% of the mass, and they show no clear pattern. e on its own has precision 0.03. Firing when the token being output is x (rather than input) has precision 0.01. None of the extra predicates I tried (output is x, input is e, x at t=1-2, x right after the first token) gave a better F1.
